title: Why LLM Recommenders Will Be AI's Biggest Consumer App — Devansh Tandon, Meta
talk_summary: A Meta research talk arguing recommendation systems follow LLM-style scaling laws and that LLM-native recommenders will be a huge consumer app. The only transferable engineering ideas are token-efficiency via pointer/semantic-ID outputs and a shared-base-model-plus-light-per-surface-finetune architecture.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of generating full content tokens at inference, the model outputs a compact semantic ID that points to existing content, so each output token is an address rather than manufactured text.
takeaways.evidence_quote: content feeds are significantly cheaper up to 100 times or more cheaper than AI chat apps because they're decoding pointers to content rather than content itself
takeaways.numbers: up to ~100x cheaper inference per hour of engagement; 3-min video compressed from ~10,000 tokens to ~10 tokens

takeaways.technique: Compress long histories into stable compact tokens
takeaways.what_they_do: They tokenize content into stable semantic IDs so long user-interaction sequences fit in the context window instead of blowing it up with raw content.

takeaways.technique: Shared base model + light per-surface fine-tuning
takeaways.what_they_do: Most compute is spent on one shared base model; each product surface only gets light surface-specific fine-tuning rather than a from-scratch model.

takeaways.technique: Agentic loop: plan, retrieve, rank, critique, refine
takeaways.what_they_do: Describes an emerging paradigm where agents orchestrate a loop of planning, retrieval, ranking, critiquing and refining outputs instead of a single forward pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can imagine a loop where agents plan, retrieve, rank and then critique the recommendations. They can refine them by calling models again
